claims.claim: The model struggled to describe combat because it had no combat-state or map-placement information; DMs split between using output verbatim, mining vivid phrases, and rewriting entirely.
claims.source: CALYPSO: LLMs as Dungeon Masters' Assistants (Zhu, Martin, Head, Callison-Burch; AIIDE 2023) — ar5iv full text
claims.quote: the model struggled sometimes to describe combat
claims.page: CALYPSO: LLMs as Dungeon Masters' Assistants (Zhu, Martin, Head, Callison-Burch; AIIDE 2023) — ar5iv full text

claims.claim: When a monster had only numeric stats and no published prose (real animals, golems), the summariser had nothing to draw on and produced unhelpful text until prompted to use 'thematic commonsense'.
claims.source: CALYPSO: LLMs as Dungeon Masters' Assistants (Zhu, Martin, Head, Callison-Burch; AIIDE 2023) — ar5iv full text
claims.page: CALYPSO: LLMs as Dungeon Masters' Assistants (Zhu, Martin, Head, Callison-Burch; AIIDE 2023) — ar5iv full text

claims.claim: In a 36-participant within-subjects study, different users produced less semantically distinct ideas with ChatGPT than with an Oblique Strategies deck (p=.038); the effect is group-level (the LLM suggests similar ideas to different people), not individual fixation.
claims.source: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text
claims.quote: less semantically distinct ideas with ChatGPT
claims.page: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text

claims.claim: Participants found that asking ChatGPT for more ideas returned repeats of the same ones.
claims.source: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text
claims.quote: When I want more, I want different more.
claims.page: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text

claims.claim: The single most common interview theme (n=10) was that ChatGPT was easier to use but less rewarding; n=8 found it less engaging.
claims.source: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text
claims.quote: easier to use but less rewarding
claims.page: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text

claims.claim: The authors attribute homogenization partly to the low inferential distance between LLM outputs and apparently complete ideas — the output arrives looking finished, so users stop diverging.
claims.source: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text
claims.quote: low inferential distance between LLM outputs
claims.page: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation (Anderson, Shah, Kreminski; C&C 2024, best paper) — arXiv full text

claims.claim: Expanding a one-sentence instruction into a story delegates most of the ~1,500 decisions a 1,500-word piece needs to the model, leaving text with an unusually low ratio of human decision-making to length.
claims.source: The Dearth of the Author in AI-Supported Writing (Kreminski; In2Writing @ CHI 2024) — PDF, text extracted locally
claims.quote: unusually sparse in terms of expressive intent per word
claims.page: The Dearth of the Author in AI-Supported Writing (Kreminski; In2Writing @ CHI 2024) — PDF, text extracted locally

claims.claim: The recurring verdict that AI output is 'soulless' reflects the sparseness of intent in the outputs that are easiest to create and therefore dominate non-enthusiasts' impressions.
claims.source: The Dearth of the Author in AI-Supported Writing (Kreminski; In2Writing @ CHI 2024) — PDF, text extracted locally
claims.quote: reflects the sparseness of intent in the outputs
claims.page: The Dearth of the Author in AI-Supported Writing (Kreminski; In2Writing @ CHI 2024) — PDF, text extracted locally

claims.claim: Experienced writers, with an ear for evocative language and an aversion to cliché, readily identify problems in AI-generated text; novices treat the machine as a creative authority and delegate more.
claims.source: The Dearth of the Author in AI-Supported Writing (Kreminski; In2Writing @ CHI 2024) — PDF, text extracted locally
claims.page: The Dearth of the Author in AI-Supported Writing (Kreminski; In2Writing @ CHI 2024) — PDF, text extracted locally

claims.claim: A tool that makes similar creative decisions in similar usage scenarios homogenizes different users' outputs in proportion to how many decisions it makes directly.

claims.claim: LLMs are effective at open-domain story generation but struggle with long-term coherence, often failing to produce a satisfying overall arc or reader experience.
claims.source: Guiding and Diversifying LLM-Based Story Generation via Answer Set Programming (Wang & Kreminski; Wordplay @ ACL 2024)
claims.quote: often failing to produce a satisfying overall story arc
claims.page: Guiding and Diversifying LLM-Based Story Generation via Answer Set Programming (Wang & Kreminski; Wordplay @ ACL 2024)

claims.claim: Compared with human-written stories, LLM stories show unoriginality in both what happens and how sentences are built.
claims.source: Guiding and Diversifying LLM-Based Story Generation via Answer Set Programming (Wang & Kreminski; Wordplay @ ACL 2024)
claims.quote: unoriginality or homogeneity in both the semantic and syntactic aspects
claims.page: Guiding and Diversifying LLM-Based Story Generation via Answer Set Programming (Wang & Kreminski; Wordplay @ ACL 2024)

claims.claim: Across ten-story sets per premise, earlier paragraphs were more homogeneous than later ones whether or not ASP guidance was used — openings converge hardest.

claims.page: Guiding and Diversifying LLM-Based Story Generation via Answer Set Programming (Wang & Kreminski; Wordplay @ ACL 2024)

claims.claim: PPO/DPO-style post-training raises output quality but lowers diversity; instruction-tuned models cluster as high-reward, low-diversity, and a deviation-weighted objective was needed to reach human-dataset diversity.
claims.source: Modifying Large Language Model Post-Training for Diverse Creative Writing (Chung, Kreminski et al.; COLM 2025)
claims.quote: high reward but with low diversity
claims.page: Modifying Large Language Model Post-Training for Diverse Creative Writing (Chung, Kreminski et al.; COLM 2025)

claims.claim: Across 819 GPT-4 vs 819 human movie synopses, LLM stories are homogeneously positive and lack tension: GPT-4 produced 'Man in Hole' arcs over 50% of the time versus 28% for humans, and 'Riches to Rags' 1.3% versus 14.6%.
claims.source: Are Large Language Models Capable of Generating Human-Level Narratives? (Tian et al.; EMNLP 2024)
claims.quote: LLM stories are homogeneously positive and lack tension
